6. On perusal of the judgment and order of the court of trial below dated 11.8.98 it transpires that the court of trial after hearing both sides and considering the documents filed by both sides came to a conclusion that plaintiffs and defendants are co-sharers in suit plot Nos. 525/519. Moreover, the defendants have been able to file Mutation Khatian No. 195 and rent payment receipts and the previous record of right, also stands in the name of their predecessors and thus did not believe the case of the plaintiffs rather held." If a co-sharer chooses to make a construction at his own risk he should not be restrained from making construction. If any portion of such construction falls in the Saharn of another co-sharer, possession thereof shall be given to the allottee by demolition of the construction." The learned Court of trial also found balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of the defendants and rejected the prayer for temporary injunction and vacated ex-parte temporary injunction order dated 18.2.98. 

 16. In view of the above decision and the fact that the Plaintiffs name appeared in the Mutation Khatian, S.A. Khatian and they have filed rent payment receipts. These documents prima facie proved title followed by exclusive possession of the defendants. Moreover the Advocate Commissioner after spot verification submitted a report staying that defendants are in possession. In my view nature and character of a suit land may be allowed to be changed pending decision of the suit on merit by improvements but no change in the nature and character of suit land which would demolish of value of the land or cause irreparable loss and prejudice to the other co-sharer should be allowed. I am further of the view that in the present day scarcity of accommodation in other areas co-sharer should not be deprived of in his possession by making construction at his risk. Over and above, I also find that claim of the plaintiffs is not simple one. It required sufficient evidence to establish their claim. Therefore, defendants cannot be restrained from making construction on the suit land taking the risk that a portion of it will be liable to be demolished if the plaintiff get a decree in future.
